families.name: Starlink Direct to Cell
families.lede: A Starlink satellite with an extra antenna that behaves like a mobile mast. Your phone sees it as just another network to roam on.

facts.v: A flat, slab-shaped body about 4.1 m across, with solar wings that span about 29 m tip to tip. About 960 kg at launch.
A phased-array antenna of about 2.7 m by 2.3 m (roughly 6 m²). SpaceX calls it a cellphone tower in space.
Very low: about 360 km up, in two groups of orbits tilted at 53° and 43°.

It borrows your own network’s 4G frequencies, so an ordinary 4G phone connects as if it were roaming. In the UK, O2 Satellite uses 5 MHz of O2’s 1800 MHz spectrum. Each satellite can point 48 beams down and listen with 16.
Texts, data for 40+ selected apps, and voice calls through apps such as WhatsApp. Ordinary (native) phone calls are a future step.
T-Mobile (US), VMO2 (UK), Rogers (Canada), One NZ, Telstra, KDDI, NTT Docomo, SoftBank, Kyivstar, Entel, Globe, Airtel Africa, Deutsche Telekom and more.

next.v: A second generation (V2) is planned with around 20 times the throughput of today’s satellites. SpaceX expects them to reach orbit during 2027.

card.v: Wings about 29 m tip to tip; phone antenna about 2.7 × 2.3 m
Texts, 40+ apps and app calls on ordinary 4G phones

families.name: BlueBird (Block 1 and Block 2)
families.lede: Few satellites, but enormous ones. Each BlueBird unfolds a huge flat antenna, so it can hear a normal phone’s weak signal from hundreds of kilometres away.

facts.v: A giant flat square panel, folded for launch and opened in orbit. The side facing Earth is covered in small antennas; the back carries solar cells.
Array about 693 sq ft (64 m²), about 1,500 kg. Launched together in September 2024.
Array about 2,400 sq ft (223 m²), more than three times bigger, and about 6,100 kg, with AST’s own AST5000 signal-processing chip.
About 520 km up, tilted at 53°.
It uses partner networks’ own mobile frequencies, mostly low-band, which travels further and gets indoors more easily. Examples: 700 MHz with Rakuten in Japan, 900 MHz with VodafoneThree in the UK.

Built for full 4G and 5G broadband. Voice calls, video calls, texts and data have been tested on unmodified phones, but there is no commercial service yet. AST is aiming for first, patchy coverage before the end of 2026.
AT&T, Verizon and Vodafone, plus Rakuten, Telus, stc and 2degrees among others.

next.v: AST is aiming for about 45 BlueBirds in orbit by mid-2027. AST says that is when service can move beyond patchy coverage.

card.v: Block 2 array about 223 m² (2,400 sq ft); Block 1 about 64 m²
Built for 4G/5G broadband; testing, not commercial yet

families.name: Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper)
families.lede: Amazon’s rival to Starlink broadband. Today’s Leo satellites talk to dishes and terminals, not to the phone in your pocket.

facts.v: Customers connect through Amazon’s own antennas (Leo Nano, Leo Pro and Leo Ultra), not with a mobile phone.
TBC. Amazon hasn’t published dimensions we could check, so our drawing is a generic flat-panel satellite.
Three layers of orbits, at 590 km, 610 km and 630 km.
High-frequency Ka-band links to customer antennas and ground stations. That is why a phone can’t use it directly.
Telecoms partners such as Vodafone, DirecTV, Herotel and Australia’s National Broadband Network.

next.v: Amazon has filed with the FCC for a separate phone network of up to 5,105 satellites using Globalstar’s spectrum, with deployment starting in 2028.

card.v: None: broadband for dishes, not phones

families.name: Lynk
families.badge: Talks to ordinary phones · small fleet
families.lede: The small one. Lynk calls its satellites ‘cell towers in space’. They are about the size of a coffee table and focus on texts and emergency alerts.

facts.v: A flat box about 1 m across and about 85 kg. That is tiny next to a Starlink or a BlueBird.
Low Earth orbit on a near-polar path (about 97°), going round roughly every 94 minutes. Exact height: TBC.

It works with standard, unmodified phones through partner networks. The merged company, Elveo, also holds rights to 60 MHz of satellite S-band spectrum and says it supports 2G, 4G, 5G and IoT devices.
Two-way text messages and emergency alerts, with a satellite passing overhead from time to time. MTN tested a voice call in South Africa in March 2025.
56 contracts with mobile networks and distribution partners in more than 60 countries. Elveo is testing with ten operators.

next.v: Elveo plans 320 new low-orbit satellites from late 2027, with commercial service in early 2028.

families.operator: Globalstar (agreed to be bought by Amazon)
families.name: Globalstar
families.badge: Only phones built for it, e.g. iPhone
families.lede: The network behind the satellite features on iPhone 14 and later. It flies much higher than the others and uses its own satellite frequencies.

facts.v: Today’s second-generation satellites weigh about 700 kg at launch and run on solar power.
About 1,414 km up, tilted at 52°. That is nearly four times as high as Starlink’s phone satellites.
It uses Globalstar’s own satellite band, not your mobile network’s, so only phones built for it can connect. The satellites act as relays, passing your message down to a Globalstar ground station.
On iPhone 14 or later: Emergency SOS, messages to friends and family, Roadside Assistance and Find My location updates. A message can take 30 seconds or more to send.
Apple. Amazon has agreed to buy Globalstar; the FCC approved the deal on 27 Oct 2026.

next.v: Nine more MDA-built replacement satellites are due on the next Globalstar launch (in our launch list). After that comes C-3, a new 48-satellite system (plus 6 spares) at 1,414 km built for phones. Launches start in 2027.

card.v: Only phones built for it: iPhone 14+ SOS, messages, Find My
